simple.meaning: צָמִיד (tsâmîyd) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a bracelet or arm-clasp ; generally, a lid.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 24:22. The surrounding context includes family, family line, offering, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָמִיד (H6781) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: צָמִיד (tsâmîyd) / H6781 is traced through Genesis 24:22, Genesis 24:30, Genesis 24:47, Numbers 19:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

When he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man. Behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands.
Every open vessel, which has no covering bound on it, is unclean.
We have brought Yahweh’s offering, what every man found: gold ornaments, armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for our souls before Yahweh.”
I decked you with ornaments, put bracelets on your hands, and put a chain on your neck.

definitions.full: H6781. tsamiyd I. צָמִיד noun masculine Gen 24:22 bracelet ( bound on wrist); — absolute ׳צ Num 31:50 ; plural צְמִידִים Gen 24:22 +; — bracelet 24:22 , 30 , 47 (J), Num 31:50 (P); in figure Ezek 16:11 ; 23:42 . II. צָמִיד noun [masculine] cover, of vessel , Num 19:15 . צַמָּה see צמם .
